about: Powerscourt Estate (paid) and Waterfall (separate park), Co. Wicklow. Round 2, garden-first method. Zero trees verified: powerscourt.com (403 to curl and WebFetch, Cloudflare; Wayback copies of /our-garden/trees/, /events/tree-trail/ and /visit-us/ load via curl) names only the tallest tree and three champions without placing any, and the 26-tree trail map is a PDF/image not reachable. Overpass unreachable. House centre 53.18472,-6.18694 (Powerscourt's own GPS line).

leads.name: Tallest tree in Ireland, River Walk Douglas fir
leads.age_register: 100-150 (register band, 2009); owner: a line of Douglas firs on the estate about 150 years old
leads.source: powerscourt.com/our-garden/trees/ (Wayback 2025 copy): 'The River Walk at Powerscourt features the tallest tree in Ireland, a Douglas Fir ... 61.5 metres, or 202 ft'; Irish Examiner 2013-11-05 (arid-30612237) same figure; Heritage Trees of Ireland, Tree Council of Ireland / Aubrey Fennell (NBDC dataset 27, CC BY 4.0), survey 2009
leads.reason: No photo or exact pin in reach: the tree is real and on the owner's page, but nothing seen places THE tallest trunk. Register row 437 is the only Douglas fir 'exceptional specimen' at Powerscourt (53.17121,-6.19726, near the Dargle at Onagh Bridge, ~1.5 km SW of the house), a plausible but unproven match for the River Walk tree; the 100-150 year band and the 2013 recognition date are not tied to it. Height disputed in search summaries (56 m UCC page, 57.5 m Tree Register survey; NOT seen on a fetched page) and an Avondale (Wicklow) Douglas fir is reported at 61.3 m, 2018, so the 'tallest in Ireland' crown may be contested (superlatives.py). Needs: the trail map or a geotagged photo of the River Walk tree, or the Tree Register of Ireland champion entry. Access: paid garden entry (prices not seen); River Walk path status not seen.
